newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., finalizes $72.5 mln arena deal.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., finalizes $72.5 mln arena deal.

text.p: Sacramento plans to come to market later this week with $72.5 million of bonds to refinance its basketball arena, city officials said.
Sacramento Treasurer Thomas Friery said the lease revenue bonds should be priced on July 17.
"We'll test the market here come Thursday," he said.
MBIA Inc has agreed to insure the bonds, which will reset quarterly. Merrill Lynch & Co will be the lead underwriter.
A Sacramento County Superior Court ruled in June that the financing was legal, eliminating court challenges that threatened to scuttle the arena deal.
The Sacramento City Council approved the bond plan in February to keep the National Basketball Association's Sacramento Kings from leaving the city.
With the proceeds of the bond sale, the city will refinance $51.5 million of Arco Arena debt, where the Kings play. The remaining bond proceeds will be used to refinance other franchise debts.
